title: Stonegate Works onramp field notes
text:
Stonegate Works onramp field notes

Call summary (2025-09-14):
- Attendees: Ava (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood infra), Priya (Redwood solutions), Marcus (Stonegate Works CTO), Leila (Stonegate platform lead), Arun (Stonegate security).
- High-level ask: integrate an LLM-powered dispatch assistant into Stonegate’s field ops portal. Must run in customer VPC (private deployment) or air-gapped on-prem for regulatory customers. Primary goals are improved routing suggestions, automated incident summaries, and semantic search over repair notes.

Key non-functional constraints / requirements:
- Latency SLO: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 300ms for single-turn generate requests under normal load. Extremely latency-sensitive for live dispatch flows.
- Throughput: steady-state ~130–200 requests/sec during peak; burst up to ~450 req/s for 10–15 minute windows.
- Context size: typical conversational + recent telemetry ~2k–6k tokens; some long doc lookups up to ~32k tokens (archival retrieval).
- Data security: must not leave customer VPC. All logs encrypted at rest; integration with their KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, keys managed by customer) required. SOC2 + ISO27001 needed; some customers demand extra audit trails.
- Cost sensitivity: target cost envelope for Hosted-equivalent is limited; they expect Redwood to propose quantized model variants and batching to control unit cost.
- Legal: cannot persist raw PII logs beyond 7 days; need redaction pipeline or prompt-layer filtering.

Model / infra preferences mentioned by customer:
- Prefer open model family (they asked about Llama-/Mistral-style variants) with 13B–30B options; will consider quantized FP16/INT8 builds.
- Want streaming responses for interactive UI, with option to fall back to non-streaming for auditability.
- Suggestion to keep small on-node cache for recent conversations (prefix/KV caching).

Technical gotchas / risks called out in conversation:
- Tokenization mismatches: Stonegate has lots of mixed-format logs (CSV chunks, device telemetry), punctuation-heavy entries — may blow up token counts and hurt latencies. Need a tokenizer audit on sample logs.
- Long-document retrieval: embedding+search pipeline must support chunking and reranking without inflating end-to-end latency. They explicitly worried about synchronous retrieval on critical path.
- Multiregion peering: some sites are in EU and APAC; VPC peering across regions may be slow—need to propose edge routing or regional replicas.
- Licensing/compliance: some customers of Stonegate (govt contractors) insist on air-gapped deploys and require an uplift in support SLAs.
- Monitoring: they want token-level cost telemetry routed to their billing system; will likely need per-route export hooks or webhook integrations.

Preliminary architecture ideas (informal):
- Private Redwood control plane (managed) + customer-hosted inference plane inside their VPC (Redwood Private). Control plane orchestrates model versions but never sees payloads.
- Inference nodes: 3x H100-ish or 4x A100-80GB (quantized 13B) for pilot to hit p50/p95 targets with batching. Autoscale policy: keep buffer of 20–30% capacity for bursts.
- KV/prefix caching: local node cache for active conversations; global Redis-like cache only for non-sensitive metadata.
- Retrieval: async retrieval microservice that pre-fetches candidate passages and attaches top-K to prompt; for critical-request path use cached/recent docs only.
- Fallback: smaller 3B quantized model for degraded paths to preserve availability and reduce cost.

Pilot scope proposal (2-week pilot):
- Week 0–1: deploy 3-node quantized 13B cluster in Stonegate dev VPC, integrate KMS and test encryption/egress policies. Import small set (1–2 weeks) of anonymized logs and run tokenizer audit.
- Week 2: run live traffic slice (10% of dispatchers) for 48–72h, collect latency/cost metrics, run output-quality evals against 100 prompt set.
- Deliverables: latency/cost dashboard, tokenizer report, prompt-set quality report, roll-forward checklist.

Immediate action items (owners / due dates):
- Request from Stonegate: 48h sample of production logs (anonymized) + schema for telemetry and note formats — Owner: Leila (Stonegate) — Due: 2025-09-18.
- Tokenizer audit on sample logs — Owner: Jordan Li (Redwood infra) — Due: 2025-09-19.
- Draft pilot sizing + cost estimate (three infra options: H100, A100-80GB, and cheaper 8x-small GPUs + quantized 3B fallback) — Owner: Ava Martinez — Due: 2025-09-20.
- Security checklist and KMS integration plan + sample endpoints for key rotation — Owner: Priya Patel — Due: 2025-09-22.
- Legal intro and NDA follow-up (Stonegate want SOC2 evidence + contract tweaks) — Owner: Marcus Reed (account lead) — Due: 2025-09-21.
- Create Confluence proposal page with architecture diagram + canary plan — Owner: Ava Martinez — Due: 2025-09-20 (link to be sent to Stonegate).

Open questions to clarify with Stonegate:
1) Precise PII classification rules — what fields must be redacted? (PII -> 7-day retention requirement applies only to customer-facing logs or all logs?)
2) Do they want synchronous long-doc retrieval on critical path or prefer async prefetch with best-effort freshness?
3) Acceptable fallback model latency/cost tradeoffs (explicit numeric targets for degraded mode).
4) Which regions require local replicas (US-EAST, EU-WEST, AP-SOUTHEAST?)
5) Who is the platform engineer contact for firewall/subnet work (we need a point to coordinate peering and route tables).

Notes-to-self / reminders: 
- Bring up tokenizer edge cases early; if tokenization doubles expected token counts, it kills p95 targets.
- Prepare two prompt templates: one optimized for short-latency interactive answers, one for longer summarization (deferred).
- Build an eval harness that runs both streaming and non-streaming response generation to compare UX + audit logs.
- Add a cookie-cutter KMS integration doc we can hand to Stonegate security.

Next meeting: schedule 30–45m to walk architecture diagram and pilot economics; target week of 2025-09-22. Marcus to propose times.

Quick decision log:
- Stonegate leaning heavily to private deployment; they will escalate if air-gapped is required for specific customers.
- They accept initial use of quantized open models; want a roadmap to a larger model if quality regressions seen.

Status: draft — will update after tokenizer audit and sample log ingest.
